description: Somos un grupo con el objetivo de crear un juego didáctico para niños a partir de 5 años. Nos interesa sumar personas creativas, comprometidas y con ganas de aportar nuevas ideas. Son especialmente bienvenidos quienes tengan conocimientos o experiencia en programación, desarrollo de videojuegos, diseño gráfico, ilustración, animación, narración de historias, investigación científica o diseño de experiencias educativas.
summary:
NASA left rovers, landers, and probes on the Moon and Mars, and their stories are fascinating. But the information about them is usually technical and dull for young children, so space-loving kids rarely find out what became of these relics.
We built a children’s video game, The Quiet Signal, where kids explore the Moon and then Mars, find each abandoned relic, and discover how it ended up there. Instead of reading, they explore, and each object tells its own story based on real NASA missions.
We make the history of space exploration fun and accessible for kids ages 6 and up, and easy to share as a family. The game turns hard-to-read NASA data into an experience, and it keeps these missions from being forgotten.
We design for very young children instead of simplifying adult content. Our game tells stories rather than listing facts, and each relic becomes a character with something to say. “Abandoned, but not forgotten” is at the heart of our project.
details:
It is a platformer video game for school-age kids who love space. Through play, they learn the stories of several pieces of equipment NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars. Players explore the maps, find each piece of equipment, and discover its story in a fun and interactive way.

It turns information that is often technical and dull into an enjoyable experience. Kids learn about real NASA missions while playing at their own pace. It also gives teachers an engaging resource to bring these topics into the classroom. We hope to help teachers make learning easier for children by giving them a tool that captures kids’ attention and makes it easier to teach the history of space exploration.

To develop it, we used Claude, GitHub Copilot, and NASA resources included in our challenge. We programmed it with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Phaser 3, and worked in Visual Studio.

Our project is creative because it turns discarded equipment into characters with a story to tell. Instead of reading facts, players discover them by exploring which turns the history of real missions into an adventure.

We considered the attention span of today's children. That is why we designed everything to capture and hold the attention of elementary-school kids, ages from 6 to 12: interactive play, short stories, and an eye-catching design.
